title: Vertebrates and Invertebrates
seo_title: Primary 5 Basic Science and Technology: Vertebrates and Invertebrates Worksheets (NERDC)
standard_code: Primary 5 Basic Science and Technology: Living and Non-Living Things
standard_text: Animals are classified into vertebrates (fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds, mammals) and invertebrates (insects, spiders, mollusks, worms and others) using their features. (summary of the Basic Science and Technology curriculum, Primary 5, theme: Living and Non-Living Things)
meta_desc: Free Primary 5 Basic Science and Technology worksheets (NERDC curriculum, theme: Living and Non-Living Things): biodiversity and groups, vertebrates, invertebrates, plants and fungi, classification keys and sorting living things. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Scientists group living things by features.
key_sub: Vertebrates have a backbone; keys split groups in two at each step.
body_html:
How to think about it

Biodiversity is the variety of living things. Classification sorts them into groups by shared features.

  • Kingdoms include animals, plants and fungi (and tiny living things like bacteria).
  • Vertebrates have a backbone: fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals.
  • Invertebrates have no backbone: insects, spiders, worms, snails.
  • A dichotomous key asks yes-or-no questions to name a living thing.
Example

A frog has moist skin and starts life as a tadpole. Which group is it in?

moist skin

water then land

Answer: amphibians

Example

Is a spider an insect?

count the legs: 8

Answer: no, it is an arachnid

Common mistakes

  • Thinking spiders are insects.
  • Thinking whales are fish (they are mammals).
  • Thinking fungi are plants.

faq.a: The variety of living things in an area, from tiny insects to large trees and animals.

faq.q: What is the difference between vertebrates and invertebrates?
faq.a: Vertebrates have a backbone. Invertebrates do not.

faq.q: How does a dichotomous key work?
faq.a: It gives two choices at each step. You choose the one that fits until you reach the name.

items.q: An animal has eight legs and two body parts. Which group does it belong to?
items.e: This is a key characteristic of arachnids.

items.q: Which group does a lobster belong to?
items.e: A lobster is a crustacean.

items.q: Mushrooms do not make their own food and grow from spores. Which kingdom are they in?
items.e: Fungi absorb food from what they grow on.

items.q: Which group are spiders in?
items.e: Spiders have two body parts and eight legs.

items.q: Which feature do all insects share?
c: six legs and three body parts
items.e: Spiders have eight legs, so they are not insects.

items.q: An animal lives in water, breathes with gills and has scales and fins. Which group does it belong to?
items.e: This is a key characteristic of fish.

items.q: Which group of living things does the bacteria in our gut belong to?
items.e: Bacteria are living things too small to be seen without a microscope.

items.q: Which group of living things does a pandan plant belong to?
items.e: Plants are green and make their own food.

items.q: Which group of living things does a hibiscus plant belong to?
items.e: Plants are green and make their own food.

items.q: Which group of living things does yeast belong to?
items.e: Fungi cannot make their own food. They feed on dead or decaying matter and reproduce by spores.

items.q: Which group does a seal belong to?
items.e: Seals have fur, breathe air and feed their young on milk.

items.q: Which group has a backbone?
items.e: Fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals have backbones.

items.q: A painted turtle has dry scaly skin and lays eggs on land. Which vertebrate group is it in?
items.e: Reptiles have dry scales.

items.q: Which group does a scorpion belong to?
items.e: A scorpion is an arachnid.

items.q: Which group of living things does a mushroom belong to?
items.e: Fungi cannot make their own food. They feed on dead or decaying matter and reproduce by spores.

items.q: Which group of living things does a grass plant belong to?
items.e: Plants are green and make their own food.

items.q: Which group does a spider belong to?
items.e: Spiders have 8 legs and 2 body parts: arachnids, not insects.

items.q: An animal has eight jointed legs and no antennae. Which group does it belong to?
items.e: This is a key characteristic of arachnids.

items.q: Why do scientists classify living things?
c: to group them by shared features so they are easier to study
items.e: Classification shows how living things are related.

items.q: Which group does a puffin belong to?
items.e: A puffin is a bird.

items.q: A spring peeper lives in water as a tadpole and on land as an adult. Which group is it in?
items.e: Amphibians change from water to land.

items.q: What is biodiversity?
c: the number of rocks in an area
the variety of living things in an area
items.e: More kinds of living things means more biodiversity.

items.q: Is a wasp a vertebrate or an invertebrate?
items.e: Vertebrates have a backbone; invertebrates do not. A wasp is an insect.

items.q: Which group of mammals does the flying fox belong to?
items.e: A placental mammal is a mammal whose young grow inside the mother, fed by a placenta.

items.q: Which of these animals is a bird?
items.e: An eagle is a bird.

items.q: Is a slow worm a vertebrate or an invertebrate?
items.e: Vertebrates have a backbone; invertebrates do not. A slow worm is a legless lizard with dry, scaly skin: a reptile.

items.q: Which of these animals is a crustacean?
items.e: A crab is a crustacean.

items.q: A dichotomous key gives two choices at each step. What do you do?
c: pick the choice that matches the living thing and follow it
items.e: Each step splits the group in two.

items.q: Is an octopus a vertebrate or an invertebrate?
items.e: Vertebrates have a backbone; invertebrates do not. An octopus has a soft body: a mollusc.

items.q: Is a lobster a vertebrate or an invertebrate?
items.e: Vertebrates have a backbone; invertebrates do not. A lobster is a crustacean.

items.q: Which of these animals is a reptile?
items.e: A lizard is a reptile.

items.q: Which group of mammals does the Tasmanian devil belong to?
items.e: A marsupial is a mammal whose young grow in a pouch.

items.q: Is a salamander a vertebrate or an invertebrate?
items.e: Vertebrates have a backbone; invertebrates do not. A salamander is an amphibian.

items.q: Is a seahorse a vertebrate or an invertebrate?
items.e: Vertebrates have a backbone; invertebrates do not. Seahorses have gills and fins: fish.

items.q: Is an adder a vertebrate or an invertebrate?
items.e: Vertebrates have a backbone; invertebrates do not. An adder is a reptile.

items.q: Which of these animals is an insect?
items.e: A grasshopper is an insect.

items.q: Which group of mammals does the sugar glider belong to?
items.e: A marsupial is a mammal whose young grow in a pouch.

items.q: Which of these animals is an arachnid?
items.e: Harvestmen have 8 legs: arachnids.

items.q: Which kingdom makes its own food using sunlight?
items.e: Plants are producers.

items.q: Which of these animals is a mollusc?
items.e: A mussel is a mollusc.

items.q: Which group of animals does an ant belong to?
items.e: An ant has three body parts and six legs, so it belongs to the insects.

items.q: An animal breathes through lungs and lays eggs with leathery shells on land. Which group does it most likely belong to?
items.e: An animal that breathes through lungs and lays eggs with leathery shells on land belongs to the reptiles.

items.q: An animal lays eggs in water and its young breathe through gills. Which group does it most likely belong to?
items.e: An animal that lays eggs in water and its young breathe through gills belongs to the amphibians.

items.q: An animal has a beak and two wings. Which group does it most likely belong to?
items.e: An animal that has a beak and two wings belongs to the birds.

items.q: Which group of animals does a parrot belong to?
items.e: A parrot has feathers, so it belongs to the birds.

items.q: How many legs does a slug have?
items.e: Counting legs is a quick way to group minibeasts: insects 6, spiders 8.

items.q: Which group of animals does a duck belong to?
items.e: A duck has feathers, so it belongs to the birds.

items.q: Is a fir tree a flowering or a non-flowering plant?
items.e: A fir tree does not make flowers. It reproduces with seeds in cones.

items.q: How many legs does a harvestman have?
items.e: Counting legs is a quick way to group minibeasts: insects 6, spiders 8.

items.q: An animal breathes through gills all its life. Which group does it most likely belong to?
items.e: An animal that breathes through gills all its life belongs to the fish.

items.q: An animal feeds its young with milk. Which group does it most likely belong to?
items.e: An animal that feeds its young with milk belongs to the mammals.

items.q: Is a moss a flowering or a non-flowering plant?
items.e: A moss does not make flowers. It reproduces with spores.

items.q: Which group of animals does a sparrow belong to?
items.e: A sparrow has feathers, so it belongs to the birds.

items.q: An animal has a pair of feelers (antennae) and three body parts. Which group does it most likely belong to?
items.e: An animal that has a pair of feelers (antennae) and three body parts belongs to the insects.

items.q: How many legs does an ant have?
items.e: Counting legs is a quick way to group minibeasts: insects 6, spiders 8.

items.q: Which group of animals does an elephant belong to?
items.e: An elephant has hair or fur, so it belongs to the mammals.

items.q: An animal has feathers. Which group does it most likely belong to?
items.e: An animal that has feathers belongs to the birds.

items.q: Which group of animals does a mousedeer belong to?
items.e: A mousedeer has hair or fur, so it belongs to the mammals.

items.q: How many legs does a beetle have?
items.e: Counting legs is a quick way to group minibeasts: insects 6, spiders 8.

items.q: Is a horsetail a flowering or a non-flowering plant?
items.e: A horsetail does not make flowers. It reproduces with spores.

items.q: A quadrat survey found: species A 15, species B 4, species C 5, species D 3. Calculate Simpson's index of diversity, D = 1 − Σn(n − 1)/N(N − 1).
What is the common name of Felis catus?
items.e: Felis catus: cat.

items.q: Would you find many woodlice on top of a wall in the sun?
c: No, woodlice dry out in bright, warm places.
Yes, they like dark, damp places.
items.e: Woodlice need damp places to stop them drying out.

items.q: Which word best describes the forest at Bukit Timah itself, where the living things are found?
items.e: A habitat is the place where organisms live.

items.q: Which question could you use in a key to separate an earthworm from a ladybird?
c: Is it nice to look at?
items.e: A good key question has a clear yes or no answer that is different for the two animals.

items.q: Would you find many woodlice in the soil?
c: No, woodlice dry out in bright, warm places.
Yes, they like dark, damp places.
items.e: Woodlice need damp places to stop them drying out.

items.q: What is the common name of Columba livia?
items.e: Columba livia: pigeon.

items.q: Which word best describes the school field itself, where the living things are found?
items.e: A habitat is the place where organisms live.

items.q: Where are you most likely to find a beetle?
c: in a web in a hedge
in a nest under a paving slab
items.e: Minibeasts live in the microhabitat that gives them what they need.

items.q: Which question could you use in a key to separate a bee from a snail?
c: Does it have exactly eight legs?
Is it nice to look at?
items.e: A good key question has a clear yes or no answer that is different for the two animals.

items.q: Which word best describes all the different plants and animals living in the school field?
items.e: A community is all the populations living together in a habitat.

items.q: Which word best describes one water lily in the pond?
items.e: One living thing is an organism, not a population.

items.q: Which word best describes one earthworm in the rotting log?
items.e: One living thing is an organism, not a population.

items.q: Where are you most likely to find a ladybird?
c: under a log or a stone
in a nest under a paving slab
on the leaves of a plant
items.e: Minibeasts live in the microhabitat that gives them what they need.

items.q: In the hierarchy of classification, which taxon comes directly above genus?
items.e: Domain, kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species.

items.q: Which is the scientific name for dog?
items.e: Canis familiaris: dog.

items.q: Which animal does NOT belong with the others: adder, crab, lobster, woodlouse?
items.e: The other three are crustaceans; an adder is one of the reptiles.

items.q: A newly found animal has fur, breathes air and feeds its young milk, but lives in the sea. How should it be classified?
items.e: Classify by characteristics, not by where it lives.

items.q: Which animal does NOT belong with the others: cod, scorpion, spider, tick?
items.e: The other three are arachnids; a cod is a fish.

items.q: Blessing's key asks 'Is it big?' Why is this a poor question?
c: Big is not exact, so different people may answer differently.
items.e: Use measurable features.

items.q: Which animal does NOT belong to the same group as the others: cow, dolphin, owl, dugong?
items.e: The others are mammals. An owl belongs to the birds.

items.q: Why might two scientists classify the same plant differently at first?
c: They might choose different characteristics to group by.
items.e: Classification is based on chosen features.
